g.text: Binary Search Tree
What is a Binary Tree?
A binary tree is a data structure in which
each node has at most two children:
- A left child
- A right child
It does not place any specific rules on the
values stored in the nodes — it's just a
structure.
Binary Search Tree
A Binary Search Tree is a special kind of
binary tree that follows a sorting property,
called the BST property.
🔍 The Binary Search Tree Property:
For every node in the tree:
All values in the left subtree of
that node must be less than or equal
to the node’s value.
All values in the right subtree of
that node must be greater than or equal
to the node’s value.
✅ This property must be true recursively for
every node and its subtrees in the tree.
The left subtree of a node is itself a BST.
The right subtree of a node is itself a BST.
✅ Real-Life Analogy:
Think of a bookshelf sorted by book titles:
Books to the left of any shelf are alphabetically earlier or same as the current book.
Books to the right are alphabetically later or same.
This allows you to find any book quickly using a divide-and-conquer approach — like BST search!
Inorder traversal - Ascending Order
